title: Rugged tablet for MaintainX: UK buyer's guide
meta_description: MaintainX publishes Android 7.0 or later, 6GB RAM recommended. The Tuga A10 (Android 14, 8GB RAM, IP68) meets both and runs the Android app.
intro: MaintainX is a cloud CMMS and enterprise asset management platform covering work orders, preventive maintenance, assets, checklists and inspections, parts inventory and meter readings. The vendor says it is used by over 14,000 companies, lists industries from general manufacturing, food and beverage and automotive through to facility management, fleet maintenance, distribution centres and hospitality, and states on its own site that it has joined Autodesk. Maintenance managers plan and assign work from the web application; technicians carry out that work from the mobile app.

On the floor or on site, the mobile app is where the field features live. The vendor documents offline mode, QR code and barcode scanning through the device camera, in-app photo capture and the work order timer as mobile-only, and its Google Play listing describes scanning a QR code on an asset to open its maintenance history, work orders and safety protocols. That means a device carried round a plant all shift, put down on concrete, splashed near wet processes and left in a van overnight, which is where a consumer tablet with a glass back and an unrated case tends to fail early.

This page sets out what MaintainX publishes about the devices it runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a UK maintenance or engineering team can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

requirements.requirement: Platform: Android 7.0 (Nougat) or later with Google Play access
requirements.detail: The vendor's Supported Devices page states Android 7.0 (Nougat) or later with access to the Google Play Store, and iOS 16.4 or later for Apple devices. The Google Play listing for MaintainX - CMMS & EAM (package com.commas.client, version 5.43 at the time of checking, minimum API level 24) shows device chips for Phone and Tablet. Enterprise plan customers whose devices lack Google Play access can distribute the app through an MDM solution.

requirements.requirement: Memory and storage: 4GB RAM minimum, 6GB or more recommended
requirements.detail: The same page gives a RAM minimum of 4GB and a recommendation of 6GB or more, with 150 to 200MB of available storage as the minimum and 300MB or more recommended. An older troubleshooting article still quotes 2GB or more; the Supported Devices page is the current figure.

requirements.requirement: Offline mode is mobile app only, and the device must be online first
requirements.detail: Technicians can update work orders while offline or on limited connectivity. The app stores a cache of work orders on the device; you choose how many to cache in Offline Settings, and eligible work orders are added by due date, soonest first. Offline mode activates automatically when the app cannot connect, or can be switched on manually with the Is Offline toggle in Offline Settings. You must connect to the internet first so the cache can be created or updated, and you cannot switch organisations while offline. When you reconnect and turn offline mode off, cached work orders sync automatically or manually depending on the Update cache setting (Manually, or Connected to any network). Offline mode is available on all four plans but marked Not available on web.

requirements.requirement: QR code and barcode scanning uses the device camera, in the mobile app only
requirements.detail: MaintainX can scan both QR codes and barcodes but can only display and generate QR codes. Scanning is listed among the mobile-only features alongside in-app photo capture and the work order timer; none of these is available in the web application. No support for a dedicated hardware scan engine or an external scanner is documented, so on any device the scan path is the camera.

requirements.requirement: Windows: no native app, desktop browser only
requirements.detail: No native Windows app or Microsoft Store listing is published. Windows users run the web application at app.getmaintainx.com, which the vendor says works best and is tested on the last 5 versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Opera and the last 3 major versions of Safari. The vendor warns that MaintainX might not display correctly on mobile browsers and recommends the mobile application on handheld devices. Reporting, Purchase Orders and the Library (Work Order Templates) are web-only.

No mention of NFC or RFID reading was found on the vendor site, the help centre, the Google Play listing or the App Store listing. The only asset identification method documented is QR code and barcode scanning through the camera. The NFC radio on the Tuga A10, A8 and A6 and the optional UHF RFID reader on the Tuga W10 should not be treated as MaintainX features.

requirements.requirement: Shared devices: workstation mode on the Enterprise plan
requirements.detail: The vendor publishes no screen-size guidance. For shared devices it describes workstation mode (Enterprise plan only) for tablets and mobile devices shared across multiple shifts and for desktop and laptop devices installed on facility floors, with 4 digit PIN sign-in per user. You must be connected to the internet to log into a workstation device.

recommended.why: MaintainX's field features (offline work orders, camera QR and barcode scanning, photo capture, the work order timer) are documented as mobile-app only, so the device a technician carries needs to run the Android app, not a browser. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 against a published requirement of Android 7.0 or later, carries 8GB of RAM against a recommended 6GB or more, and has 128GB of storage against a recommended 300MB or more. Its 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen gives room for checklists and procedures, the 13MP rear camera with flash is the scan and photo path the app uses, and the IP68 and MIL-STD-810H ratings cover dust, immersion, drops and site vehicles (IP68 also makes it the better choice than the IP67 A6 for wet areas). It is the device an industrial asset-management firm has already bought from us for maintenance technicians at an aerospace manufacturer, running a different CMMS mobile app.

Requirement: readable screen for checklists and inspections. Tuga A10: 10.1 inch FHD IPS 1920 x 1200 at 350 nits with tempered glass, 680g.

recommended.why: The Tuga A8 is the middle size, an 8 inch tablet that runs the same MaintainX Android app with more checklist space than the 6 inch A6 and a smaller footprint than the 10.1 inch A10. It runs Android 12 with Google Play, above the Android 7.0 requirement but older than the A10's Android 14, and its 6GB of RAM meets the 6GB or more that MaintainX recommends with no headroom, against the A10's 8GB. Its 1000 nit screen suits outdoor and sunlit work, the 8000mAh battery is removable for long shifts, and VESA mount points and a pogo pin connector suit fleet vehicle docking. Against the A10 it is sealed to IP67 rather than IP68, has no MIL-STD rating and a lower 1280 x 800 resolution, so the A10 remains the better choice for wet areas. At £379 it costs £70 less than the A10.

recommended.why: Where technicians want something that fits a pocket or a belt holster at 277g, or work across a large estate where a swappable battery helps, the Tuga A6 runs the same MaintainX Android app on a 6 inch handheld. It runs Android 15, well above the Android 7.0 requirement, but be clear on memory: its 4GB of RAM meets MaintainX's 4GB minimum and falls below the 6GB or more the vendor recommends, so for heavy use the A10 with 8GB is the safer choice, and a trial unit is worth running first. Its 64GB of storage is well above the 300MB recommendation. The Google Play listing carries both Phone and Tablet device chips, so the phone-sized layout is one the vendor publishes for. It has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but MaintainX documents camera scanning only, so plan on the 13MP rear camera. The trade-off is screen area: a 6 inch display shows less of a long checklist or a procedure at once than the A10's 10.1 inch panel.

recommended.why: MaintainX has no native Windows app. The Tuga W10 runs Windows 11 Pro, so it can run the full MaintainX web application in desktop Chrome or Edge, which are among the browsers the vendor says it tests on, including the web-only Reporting, Purchase Orders and Library modules. That makes it a fit for a supervisor's station, a planning office, or a shared floor workstation on the Enterprise plan, and it has Ethernet and HDMI for a fixed position. It is not the device for a technician in the field: the web application has no offline mode, no camera scanning, no in-app photo capture and no work order timer, and the W10 is IP65 rather than IP68, so it is protected against water jets but not rated for immersion.

setup_steps: Create a MaintainX account at getmaintainx.com or ask your administrator to add the technician as a user in your existing organisation. The vendor offers a free Basic plan and Requester accounts are free, so a trial costs nothing on the software side.

On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install MaintainX - CMMS & EAM (package com.commas.client, developer MaintainX Inc.). Enterprise plan customers without Google Play access can distribute the app through an MDM solution instead.

Sign in on the device with the technician's account. If your organisation uses workstation mode on the Enterprise plan, the shared device is set up once and each user then logs in with a 4 digit PIN; the device must be connected to the internet to log in.

Before the first shift without connectivity, keep the device online long enough for the offline cache to build, then review the Offline Settings in the app (choose how many work orders to cache, whether to cache work orders assigned to you or to you and your teams, and whether the cache updates manually or whenever connected to any network). Offline mode also switches on automatically when the app cannot connect.
On a Tuga W10, open app.getmaintainx.com in Edge or Chrome and sign in. Use it for the web-only Reporting, Purchase Orders and Library modules; it will not scan with the camera or work offline.

For the A10 and W10, fit the charging dock where devices live between shifts, or the vehicle mounting dock for fleet and site vehicles; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

faq.q: Will MaintainX run on the Tuga A10?
faq.a: MaintainX publishes a requirement of Android 7.0 (Nougat) or later with Google Play access, 4GB RAM minimum with 6GB or more recommended, and 300MB or more of storage recommended. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play, has 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets each published figure. The Tuga A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM, 64GB) meets the Android, storage and 4GB minimum RAM figures but is below the 6GB RAM recommendation, so trial one before a fleet order. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by MaintainX; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications.

faq.q: Does MaintainX work offline on these tablets?
faq.a: Yes, in the Android mobile app. The vendor's help centre documents an offline mode on all four plans that stores a cache of work orders on the device (you choose how many) and lets technicians update them without a connection, syncing when connectivity returns. The device has to be online first so the cache can be created. Offline mode is not available in the web application, so a Tuga W10 running MaintainX in a browser cannot work offline.

faq.q: Can we scan asset QR codes and barcodes with the camera, and does NFC help?
faq.a: MaintainX documents scanning both QR codes and barcodes through the device camera in the mobile app. The Tuga A10 and A6 both have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and in both cases scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support is documented by the vendor, so do not buy it for that reason. NFC and RFID are not mentioned anywhere in the vendor's documentation, so the NFC radio on the A10, A8 and A6 and the optional UHF RFID reader on the W10 should not be bought for MaintainX.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit first, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. A single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice. Tuga Hardware is the trading name of Destello Tech Ltd and is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the £449 (A10), £349 (A6) or £649 (W10) prices. Delivery is free worldwide in 7 to 10 working days, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty. Multi-unit discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 units, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more.

faq.q: Should technicians have the 10.1 inch A10 or the 6 inch A6?
faq.a: The vendor publishes no screen-size guidance and its Google Play listing carries both Phone and Tablet device chips, so both layouts are ones it ships for. The A10's 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen shows more of a checklist, inspection form or procedure at once and suits a vehicle or charging dock. The A6 at 277g fits a pocket or belt holster, has a removable 5050mAh battery, and suits technicians who walk a large estate, but its 4GB RAM is below MaintainX's 6GB recommendation, so the A10 is the safer pick for heavy daily use. Many teams mix the two.

not_recommended_note: MaintainX has no native Windows app, so the Tuga W10 only runs the web application in a desktop browser. The vendor documents offline mode, camera QR and barcode scanning, in-app photo capture and the work order timer as mobile-only, so a W10 cannot do any of those; it suits a supervisor, planner or shared Enterprise-plan workstation, not a technician in the field. On the Android side, the only asset identification method the vendor documents is camera scanning, with no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support published, so scanning on the A10 and A6 is through the camera only (the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not a documented input). NFC and RFID are not documented by MaintainX, so the NFC on the A10, A8 and A6 and the optional UHF RFID reader on the W10 are not MaintainX features. Reporting, Purchase Orders and the Library are web-only, and the vendor advises against mobile browsers, so an Android-only team will still need a desktop or laptop for those modules. The vendor is US-based, prices in dollars and names no UK customers on its site, although it advertises UK-based EMEA sales roles and publishes a UK Modern Slavery Act statement.
